family.description: Family of ATP-grasp enzymes belonging to the R2K clade, wherein one of the absolutely-conserved lysine residues has migrated to the RAGYNA domain which is a part of the core ATP-grasp module. This family is predicted to catalyze peptide ligation reactions on protein substrates in biological conflict contexts, probably between bacteriophages and their hosts [[cite:PUB00091030]].
family.name: ATP-grasp domain, R2K clade family 3
